title: kv-cache-architecture-spec-v4-draft
summary: Draft v4: converged design for KV cache layout, memory pool organization, eviction heuristics, and fragmentation mitigation for the serving runtime. Incorporates learnings from v2/v3 and field fragments (eviction/memory-pools/fragmentation).
body:
Purpose and scope:
This document captures the v4 draft of the KV cache architecture for Redwood's serving runtime. Focus areas: physical layout (on-GPU and host-resident), memory pool segmentation, eviction policies (size- and cost-aware), fragmentation mitigation and compaction strategies, observable signals, and rollout/testing plan. This is a design + operational proposal intended for engineering review before prototyping and bench testing.

Goals and constraints:
- Maximize cache hit-rate for common production distributions while controlling tail latency and memory overhead.
- Keep per-request latency predictable (SLO: P99 token generation latency impact from cache lookup < 1ms).
- Minimize internal fragmentation and avoid frequent expensive compactions on critical path.
- Support multi-tenant isolation (per-customer limits) and model-variant pinning.
- Work within existing runtime kernel constraints (KV layouts compatible with attention code paths) and GPU memory allocators.

Key terminology:
- KV segment: contiguous memory region holding cached key/values for a set of layers/heads for a model shard.
- Entry: cached KV for a particular prefix (sequence). May be variable-sized due to cached length.
- Pool: allocator arena for KV segments (hot/warm/cold).
- Fragmentation: unused memory inside pools due to variable-sized allocations and evictions.

High-level layout:
- Hybrid layout: combine fixed-size slab arenas for small/medium entries and variable chunk allocator for large entries.
- Per-model-shard namespace: each model shard has dedicated metadata and mapping to its pools to simplify eviction and versioning.
- Host + GPU residency: metadata (hash table, LRU timestamps, reference counts) on host pinned memory; hot KV bytes resident on GPU; warm/cold on host (pinned or pageable depending on policy).
- Indexing: two-level map: (model_shard_id -> local hash table) where hash table points to segment descriptors (device pointer, length, epoch). This avoids a global lock across unrelated models.

Memory pools and allocator strategy:
1) Slab pools for small entries (<= 2KB): multiple slab classes (512B, 1KB, 2KB). Fast allocation/deallocation, minimal per-entry metadata. Slabs are placed on GPU when occupancy and access frequency justify residency.
2) Chunk allocator for medium entries (2KB - 64KB): uses first-fit within chunk pages with free lists per chunk-size-class to reduce fragmentation. Pages are multiples of 64KB.
3) Large-object allocator (>64KB): allocate full pages / mmap-style pinned host buffers and optionally migrate to GPU lazily.
4) Tiered residency policy: hot pool (GPU direct), warm pool (host pinned, available for async DMA), cold pool (host pageable or disk-backed spill for very aged entries).

Eviction policies (multi-factor heuristic):
- Cost-aware LRU variant (CALRU): eviction ranking = alpha * recency_score + beta * frequency_score + gamma * size_penalty + delta * residency_cost. Tunable coefficients (start: alpha=0.6, beta=0.2, gamma=0.15, delta=0.05).
- Size-aware preferencing: when evicting to free X bytes, prefer combinations of small entries that minimize hit-rate regression per byte. Use approximate benefit-per-byte estimate based on recent access rates.
- Hot-warm migration: entries with repeated recent accesses promoted to hot (GPU); promotion budget is rate-limited to avoid eviction thrash.
- Canary eviction window: reserve a small protected window (5% of pool) for recently promoted items to avoid immediate eviction after promotion.

Fragmentation mitigation:
- Slab pools: eliminate internal fragmentation for classes covered by slabs. Slabs reduce metadata overhead and compaction need for small entries.
- Periodic compaction for chunk allocator: background compaction threads that operate off-critical-path; compaction candidates chosen based on fragmentation ratio per page and access slack (low recent accesses). Compaction moves live entries into contiguous pages and frees fragmented pages back to pool.
- Age-based trimming: very old entries moved to cold pool or spilled to disk to release large contiguous GPU blocks for hot workloads.
- Defragmentation budget: enforce CPU/GPU time budget for compaction (e.g., max 30ms/sec per node) to avoid impacting inference throughput.
- Allocation alignment: align entries to vector-width friendly boundaries (e.g., 64B) to avoid tiny misalignment waste.

Multi-tenancy, isolation and quotas:
- Per-tenant logical sub-pools tracked in metadata with quota counters. Eviction respects tenant quotas and will first evict within tenant namespace before borrowing across tenants, unless global pressure requires cross-tenant eviction (emergency override).
- Soft limits and hard limits: soft limit triggers more aggressive eviction for the tenant; hard limit disallows further allocation and triggers reject/backpressure path.

Observability and metrics:
- Required metrics: cache_hits, cache_misses, hit_rate_by_model, bytes_resident_gpu, bytes_resident_host, fragmentation_ratio_by_pool, slab_utilization_by_class, compaction_runs/sec, avg_compaction_time, eviction_count_by_reason.
- Tracing: sample request traces should include cache_lookup_time, residency_promote_time, and eviction_candidate_reason to diagnose tail latency sources.
- Alerts: fragmentation_ratio > 0.35 for > 5m should trigger investigation; compaction backlog > 10 pending tasks triggers urgent operational alert.

Operational considerations and rollout plan:
1) Prototype: implement slab + chunk allocators in a feature branch, enable for a single low-risk model and internal traffic. Bench: measure P50/P95/P99 latency changes, GPU memory utilization, hit-rate improvements vs baseline.
2) Canary: enable for 5% production traffic on hosted API for non-critical customers with detailed logging.
3) Tune coefficients of CALRU using production telemetry and offline replay experiments.
4) Gradually enable per-tenant quotas and cold-spill to host; test behavior under forced OOM and high churn patterns.
5) Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics or earlier if failures detected.

Open questions and design decisions to finalize:
- Exact coefficient values for CALRU and whether to use ML-based benefit-per-byte estimation in v1 or v2. Recommendation: start with heuristic coefficients and add learned estimator only if TTI/regret metrics justify complexity.
- Compaction algorithm details: single-threaded vs multi-threaded GPU-assisted copy. Need perf experiments.
- Spill format for cold pool: binary serialized segments vs memory-mapped per-entry files. Evaluate impact on restore latency.
- Integration with kernel-level KV access patterns: verify that chunk boundaries and alignment are friendly to attention kernel prefetch patterns.

Testing matrix:
- Unit tests for allocator correctness, fragmentation accounting, and per-tenant accounting.
- Microbench: synthetic workloads (zipfian prefix reuse, churn-heavy, long-tail large entries) measuring hit rate, eviction churn, fragmentation, compaction overhead.
- End-to-end: latency SLO adherence under 95th and 99th percentile load with realistic traffic captured from production.

Next steps:
- Review with serving-runtime and platform-eng (this week).
- Implementation spike: slab allocator + metadata + simple CALRU (2 engineer-weeks).
- Bench harness: add simulated workloads to our perf suite and run GPU-hosted experiments.

Appendix (notes / fragments collected from earlier drafts):
- v2/v3 notes referenced: previous files showed excessive fragmentation from naive variable allocator and frequent GPU-side compactions that impacted P99. Lessons learned: favor slabization for small items; decouple compaction from critical path; prefer host spill before eager GPU compaction.
- Quick todo list: add telemetry hooks for per-entry access counters; define wire-format for host-GPU pointers; update kernel prefetch to accept non-contiguous KV segments transparently.

Comments welcome.
notes: This file is intended to sit alongside existing kv-cache spec artifacts (v2, v3, fragmentation notes). It's a draft — expect iteration after design review.
